Summarise the parameter values of a calibration

Source: R/calibration_summary.R
summarise_calibration.Rd

Summarises, for every parameter value of a calibration table, the values tried by the calibration runs: what the best runs agree on, which parameters are pushed against their bounds, where the runs that failed went, and how the values moved from one generation to the next.

Usage

summarise_calibration(
  runs,
  calib_table,
  n_best = 5,
  n_top = 20,
  relative = NULL,
  bound_tol = 0.01
)

Arguments

runs

The runs: a data frame as returned by read_calibration_runs(), or the folder to read them from.

calib_table

The calibration table of the runs, as returned by generate_calibration_table().

n_best

Number of best runs whose range is given.

n_top

Number of best runs whose median, and the number at a bound, are given.

relative

Report the parameters as factors of their starting value? NULL (default) to decide per parameter as described above, TRUE or FALSE for all, or one value per row of calib_table.

bound_tol

A value counts as at a bound when it is closer to it than this fraction of the search range (calibration scale).

Value

A list of three data frames:

  • parameters: one row per row of calib_table with name, position, start (starting value), scale ("factor" or "value"), best (best run), low and high (range of the n_best best runs), median (median of the n_top best runs), at_bound (number of the n_top best runs at a bound) and failed_shift (mean value of the failed runs minus that of the completed runs, calibration scale; NA without failed runs);

  • generations: per generation and parameter, the median of the n_best best completed runs of the generation, on the scale of parameters;

  • scores: per generation, the number of runs, of failed runs, and the best and median scores of the completed runs.

The runs without generation make the generation NA.

Details

The runs are ranked by score among those that completed. The values are reported on the model scale, either as they are ("value") or as a factor of the starting value (cur_value of calib_table, "factor"). By default, a parameter is reported as a factor when its starting value lies within its bounds, and as a value otherwise (e.g. a rate started at a placeholder 1e-12 below its search range). The statistics are computed on the calibration scale and then mapped to the model scale.

See also

read_calibration_runs(), apply_parameters() to apply the values of a run.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tbl <- generate_calibration_table(mod, "calibration.yaml")
res <- summarise_calibration("calibration_results", tbl)
res$parameters
} # }
